title: Mathematics for Data Science II
standfirst: Vectors, matrices and multivariable calculus, building on the toolkit from MFDS I.

description_paragraphs: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of linear algebra, calculus, and optimization with an emphasis on their applications in machine learning and data science.
faculty: Prof. Sarang S Sane, Department of Mathematics, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Vectors and matrices; Systems of linear equations; Determinants (Part 1 and 2).

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: Solving linear equations - determinants (Part 3), Cramer's rule, invertible coefficient matrices; Echelon form, row reduction, Gaussian elimination.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Vector spaces - introduction, properties; Linear dependence and independence.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Basis and dimension - definition, computation of bases; Rank and dimension via Gaussian elimination.

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Rank and nullity of a matrix; Linear transformations - null space (basis and nullity); Linear mappings and transformations.

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Linear transformation - matrix representations with ordered bases; Image and kernel; Computation of bases for image and kernel.

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Equivalent and similar matrices; Affine subspaces and mappings; Inner products, norms, lengths, and angles.

weeks_text.label: Week 8
weeks_text.text: Orthogonality and orthonormality; Projections; Gram-Schmidt method; Orthogonal transformations and rotations.

weeks_text.label: Week 9
weeks_text.text: Multivariate functions - visualisation; Partial and directorial derivatives; Limits and continuity; Gradient interpretation.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: Optimization concepts - steepest ascent/descent: Tangent lines and tangent hyperplanes; Critical points.

weeks_text.label: Week 11
weeks_text.text: Higher-order partial derivatives; Hessian Matrix; Local extrema in two and three variables; Differentiability of multivariable functions; Review of 'Mathematics for Data Science II'.
